solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Petition god to intervene in flood

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so the god's name goes between the letters of the petition word

parts.note: a petition is a plea, an earnest request
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: Someone prays to a deity to step in and stop rising floodwaters.
explanation.definitionFit: A flood of something is an excessive amount, an overabundance, which is what this word means.

parts.note: the Ladies is a women's toilet, a loo in British slang

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its inside letters, leaving only the first and last of space

explanation.surface: Someone visiting the women's toilets discovers a vacant, messy room.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose ends or loose papers are disordered, so the word works as a synonym of messy or slack.

indicators.note: wrapping means the canvas word is placed around the other two pieces

parts.note: living under canvas means living in a tent
tore, as in rushed along, means ran
to box is to spar, as boxers do in training

explanation.surface: A see-through canvas has been draped around a container that got ripped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheer' looks like an adjective for the canvas but is the definition; 'tore' is rushing, not ripping.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer fabric is so fine it can be seen through, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Former pupil started to play with saw

parts.note: an old boy, OB, is a former pupil of a British school
in tennis a player who served began the rally, putting the ball into play

explanation.surface: A former schoolboy took up music alongside a carpentry tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' is the past tense of see, not the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Saw, past tense of see, means noticed or watched, a synonym in the same tense.

parts.note: plain, meaning unemotional and straightforward, is matter-of-fact

explanation.surface: A remark about a flat South African landscape, perhaps the veld.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a sentence adverb meaning in fact or in reality, like actually.

clue.text: After a time, head into the wind storm

indicators.note: after says the sailing manoeuvre comes after the article and the time letter

parts.note: to tack is to sail a zigzag course, turning the bow through the wind

explanation.surface: After a while a sailor steers straight into the gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' is a verb here, as in to storm a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a position is to assault it violently, the same as attacking it.

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps
a T-junction, where one road meets another at right angles, gives T

explanation.surface: Someone at last finds the road junction on the map.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the end, after delay, just as finally does.

definitions.meaning: a light brown colour, as of suntanned skin
to ... someone's hide is to beat or thrash them, to belt them

explanation.definitionFit: Tan is a yellowish-brown shade, and colloquially to tan is to give someone a hiding.

clue.text: Adjust camera without a view of outbreak of bad behaviour

indicators.note: adjust means rearrange, so the remaining letters are shuffled
without means one letter is taken out of camera

explanation.surface: A photographer tweaks a camera that has no viewfinder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes one A from CAMERA to give CMERA, and 'Adjust' rearranges that with VIEW.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden spate of crimes in an area is an outbreak of lawless behaviour.

clue.text: It is good manners to swap hands and teeth

indicators.note: swap means the two hand letters trade places within the word
to here introduces the exchange that the swap performs

parts.note: morals are principles of right conduct, broadly good manners
the hands are right and left, abbreviated R and L

explanation.surface: Etiquette says change which hand holds your fork, and mind your dentistry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hands' are R and L, right and left; swapping them in MORALS turns good manners into teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the broad grinding teeth at the back of the mouth.

clue.text: Continent lost in ocean's not cold

indicators.note: not means the cold letter is left out of the word

parts.note: the Atlantic is an ocean; the possessive adds S
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A lost landmass lies under a sea that is not chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato's legendary island continent was said to have sunk beneath the sea.

clue.text: Part of telescope belonging to Leonard

definitions.meaning: a curved glass piece that focuses light in an optical instrument

explanation.definitionFit: A telescope gathers and focuses light through curved glass components of this kind.

indicators.note: assembly means putting the letters together anew, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A question whether a parish meeting composes verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' looks like a gathering of parishioners; it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhapsodies are effusive, enthusiastic poems or epic verses.

clue.text: Sure thing to occupy non-smoker with party rattles

parts.note: a disco is a dance party

indicators.note: to occupy is to sit inside, so the sure thing goes inside the non-smoker letters

parts.note: NS is the abbreviation for non-smoker, as in small ads
a cert is a certainty, a sure thing

explanation.surface: A sure bet takes over a smoke-free area with a party that shakes everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rattles' is a verb meaning unnerves, not baby's toys.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to unsettle or unnerve them, a synonym.

parts.note: an app is a piece of software
the phrase contracts, that is shortens, to the form aren't; the apostrophe is dropped

explanation.surface: Software agreements are not transparent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracts' looks like a noun for agreements but is a verb: 'are not' contracts to the shortened form, leaving 'clear' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means obvious or plain to see, a synonym of clear.

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: In danger, someone hands out permission.
explanation.definitionFit: A privilege can be a special right or licence granted to someone, a permission.

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a scarf is a piece of clothing worn round the neck

explanation.surface: A mark on a cropped garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a lasting mark, figuratively a blemish or stain on something.

clue.text: Tale of a new European Commission prize

parts.note: to prize something is to dote on it, treasure it

explanation.surface: A story about an EU award.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing or interesting story, a tale.

definitions.meaning: to cut food into small cubes
to play with cubes for money, as in dicing with death

explanation.definitionFit: Cooks cut vegetables into cubes this way, and the word also means to play games of chance.

clue.text: In Iran some detainees are held hostage for money

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run of words Iran some detainees

explanation.surface: A news report on hostages in Iran held for ransom payments.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive who was ransomed was held until a payment was made for release.

indicators.note: to invade means to get inside, so the bold letter goes inside

parts.note: Cain, the first murderer in Genesis, with the possessive S
B is the abbreviation for bold, as in typography

explanation.surface: A brazen intruder breaks into a killer's rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bold' is the typographic abbreviation, not a description of the intruder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabins are small rooms, especially on a ship, so chambers is a fair synonym.

parts.note: to air something is to expose it, make it public
traffic is illegal trade, such as drug smuggling

explanation.surface: Airliners as a group reveal a contraband ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means all the aircraft moving through an area, taken collectively.

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken for its sound

parts.note: to sell someone is to cheat or swindle them, as in selling a pup

explanation.surface: A con man is caught and jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell is a room in a prison, used here for prison itself.

clue.text: Stout or beer moved right to the end

indicators.note: moved means the right letter is shifted to a new position in the word

parts.note: lager is a light beer

explanation.surface: A choice between a stout and a beer that has been moved to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: move the R of the answer to the end and you get LAGER, so the beer gives the answer once its R moves forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout, describing a person, means fat or bulky, which is large.

clue.text: Is a lemon chopped up into flour?

indicators.note: chopped up means cut into pieces and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook asks whether lemon gets chopped up into the flour.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina is coarse flour ground from durum wheat.

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
us is the object form of we

explanation.surface: A duty to show affection to the speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: To owe is to be in debt, obliged to repay someone.

clue.text: Model is cantankerous when knight is exchanged for rook

indicators.note: exchanged for means one letter is swapped out and another goes in

parts.note: ornery is American slang for cantankerous
N is the chess notation for knight
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A grumpy chess model makes a trade of pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess setting is apt: knight and rook are N and R in chess notation.
explanation.definitionFit: An orrery is a clockwork model of the solar system.

indicators.note: chopping means cutting into, so one letter goes into the vegetables word

parts.note: beets are root vegetables
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe meaning take

explanation.surface: A recipe heading about cutting up vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Berets are soft round flat caps.

clue.text: Trophy cases confuse success with time

indicators.note: to confuse two things is to mix one up with the other, so the letters swap places
with pairs the two letters to be swapped

parts.note: to case a blade is to sheathe it
S stands for success, as a pass mark

explanation.surface: Trophy cabinets mix up winning with the passage of time.
explanation.walkthrough: In SHEATHES the first S and the T change places to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The urn played for in cricket Test series between England and Australia is this trophy.
